title: Scaling & High Availability in the Cloud

scenes.title: Scaling & High Availability in the Cloud
scenes.narration: Scaling adds capacity to handle load, while high availability keeps your system running through failures — both are essential for production data platforms.

scenes.title: Two Dimensions to Master
bullets: Scaling lets your system absorb more load by adding resources up or out.
High availability keeps the system serving even when components fail.
Elasticity means scaling automatically in response to real demand.
scenes.narration: Production systems must handle two distinct challenges. Scaling addresses growing load by adding capacity. High availability addresses failure by ensuring the service keeps running when parts break. Elasticity ties them together by adjusting capacity automatically as demand rises and falls.

scenes.title: Vertical vs. Horizontal Scaling
scenes.narration: Vertical scaling means moving to a larger machine, which is simple but eventually hits a hardware ceiling and often requires downtime. Horizontal scaling adds more machines and scales almost without limit, though it demands a distributed design. Most cloud-native data systems favor scaling out horizontally.

scenes.title: How Auto-Scaling Reacts
steps: Monitor a metric like CPU or queue depth
scenes.narration: Auto-scaling continuously watches a signal such as CPU usage or queue depth. It compares that signal to a target you set. When demand pushes the metric above target, it adds instances, and when demand falls, it removes them. This keeps performance steady while avoiding paying for idle capacity.

scenes.title: Defining an Auto-Scaling Policy
scenes.code:
aws application-autoscaling put-scaling-policy \
  --policy-name cpu-target \
  --service-namespace ecs \
  --resource-id service/data-cluster/etl \
  --scalable-dimension ecs:service:DesiredCount \
  --policy-type TargetTrackingScaling \
  --target-tracking-scaling-policy-configuration \
  '{"TargetValue": 60.0, "PredefinedMetricSpecification": {"PredefinedMetricType": "ECSServiceAverageCPUUtilization"}}'
scenes.narration: This command sets up target-tracking auto-scaling for a service. It tells the platform to keep average CPU utilization near sixty percent by adjusting the number of running tasks. When load climbs, tasks are added automatically, and as it eases they are removed, so the service stays responsive without constant manual tuning.

scenes.text: Scale horizontally for growth and design across zones for availability — let auto-scaling handle demand so your platform stays fast and resilient.
scenes.narration: Favor horizontal scaling to grow and distribute across zones to survive failures. Letting auto-scaling respond to real demand keeps the platform both performant and resilient without manual firefighting.
